Gilmore's remark about the "wholly executory exchange where neither 
party has yet taken any action" has not gone unnoticed. An English contracts 
scholar, Professor Patrick Atiyah, has argued that the case for enforcing such 
exchanges is not compelling and that 
"there are signs of an increasing 
reluctance to impose liability in wholly executory contracts, 
that is, on 
promises which have neither been paid for, nor relied upon." Patrick S. 
~tiyah, Promises, Morals and Law 5-6 (1981). Can you find any of those 
signs? See Melvin Eisenberg, The Bargain Principle and Its Limits, 95 Harv. 
L. Rev. 741 (1982).
